newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden not seen in EMU from 1999 - analysts poll.
newsitem.headline: Sweden not seen in EMU from 1999 - analysts poll.

text.p: A poll of analysts published by Swedish commercial bank Swedbank showed most believe Sweden would not join Europe's monetary union (EMU) from its planned 1999 start.

The poll, which surveyed around 40 analysts mostly in New York, London and Frankfurt at the end of January, showed 81 percent believed the probability of Sweden taking part in EMU from its start was less than 50 percent.
"This is not particularly surprising considering the absence of debate and clear positions of politicians at the time when the survey was carried out," Swedbank said in a statement.
Uncertainty surrounding Sweden's position towards EMU was seen as a risk for the crown, analysts said.
"The uncertainty would remain as long as the government and the Swedish parliament did not take any decision on the issue, which is expected to happen in the autumn," the bank said.
As late as August at the time of a previous poll there were questions surrounding whether or not Sweden would meet EMU criteria, but now most analysts say Sweden would meet them, the bank said.
"The main question from the panel participants is instead whether or not we will join. And if we chose to remain outside how fiscal policy will then be determined," it said.
